title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-08-18
lineage: AUD mC > Rx2 > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Historic 8/18/70 show with first‑time performances of Ripple, Brokedown Palace, Operator & Truckin' captured on a listenable audience tape.
ai_review.review: The performance is a milestone – the acoustic set shines and the electric set delivers classic early‑’70 energy with debut renditions of Ripple, Brokedown Palace, Operator and a soaring Cryptical > Other One.  The recording is an audience (AUD) capture; it’s lo‑fi and a bit boomy, but most listeners find it sufficiently clear to enjoy the historic moments.

ai_rating.rationale: The show is repeatedly praised for its historic firsts and strong playing (≈4.8/5), while the audio, though lo‑fi, is considered listenable (≈2.5/5). Weighted combination yields ~4.1 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pocket‑recorder style tape; noticeable boominess around 960 Hz, occasional muddiness, but overall audible and captures the audience ambience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set is described as brilliant and smooth; electric set builds with a powerful Cryptical > Other One, Attics and Man’s World delivering the high‑energy climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for exceptional guitar tone, vocal presence and dynamic lead work on both acoustic and electric numbers (including New Speedway Boogie).
band_member_comments.Keys: Speculation about piano player – some think Pigpen, others suggest Howard Wales or Ned Lagin; no consensus.
